title: Hybrid throughput-aware micro-batching and latency hedging for rerank endpoint
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: The rerank endpoint exhibits high tail latency in mixed workloads (varying document lengths and concurrent queries). Head-of-line blocking and oversized batches cause p95/p99 spikes, and current fixed batching window plus single-worker scheduling is inefficient for short queries or bursty traffic. Goal: Reduce p95/p99 latency for rerank while preserving or improving overall throughput and GPU utilization, and provide per-customer SLA-aware timeout controls. Approach: 1) Implement a hybrid batching scheduler that composes two modes: (a) micro-batches (sub-50ms collection window or N small requests) prioritized for low-latency requests; (b) throughput batches that aggregate larger requests up to token/worker limits for high-efficiency paths. The scheduler switches modes based on current queue length, token distribution, and target SLOs. 2) Add latency hedging: when a request approaches its configured deadline (percent of SLO), spawn speculative execution on a second worker with independent micro-batch timing and return the earliest result, canceling the other execution. 3) Token-aware partitioning: compute estimated token cost per request and bound per-batch total tokens; prefer grouping similar-length requests to reduce padding inefficiency and KV cache thrashing. 4) Adaptive per-customer timeouts and routing: allow customers to specify soft/hard SLOs; controller adjusts batching window and hedging aggressiveness accordingly; default progressive policy for free-tier vs enterprise. 5) Backpressure & graceful degradation: enforce per-worker outstanding request caps and emit 429 when queue cannot be accepted; provide informative retry-after headers. 6) Integrate with KV prefix cache: short-circuit reranks for repeated prefixes and serve cached rerank scores where applicable. Metrics and observability: add p50/p90/p95/p99 for end-to-end latency, batch formation delay, scheduling overhead, tokens-per-batch, GPU utilization, hedged-success-rate, and extra-cost-per-hedge. Create dashboards and alerts for regression (>10% increase in cost or >15% regression in p99). Acceptance criteria: - p95 latency reduced by at least 25% and p99 reduced by at least 40% on synthetic mixed-length workload compared to baseline. - No more than 5% regression in overall throughput (tokens/sec) at 95% load. - Feature flags and canary rollout are implemented; canary customers observe no functional regressions. - End-to-end tests and chaos tests for worker kill/queue pressure are added. - Design and implementation reviewed by runtime and infra teams. Trade-offs considered: hedging reduces tail latency but increases GPU utilization and cost; we will make hedging configurable per-customer and bounded by a hedging budget. Grouping similar-length requests improves efficiency but may increase latency for outliers; micro-batching prioritization mitigates this.
